text: Migraine
explanation_or_correction: Draft educational reference: MedlinePlus, https://medlineplus.gov/migraine.html. Review scope, clinical red flags and teaching level with Lavin.

text: Migraine features: Migraine as a neurological headache disorder; common features and differences in symptom patterns.
Which statement best describes migraine?
option_A: It only affects the jaw joint
option_B: Migraine is always the same as a short, mild tension headache
option_C: It is a headache disorder that may include nausea and sensitivity to light or sound
option_D: It is caused only by a head injury
explanation_or_correction: Migraine is a neurological headache disorder with associated symptoms that differ by person.

text: Which symptom pattern is more characteristic of migraine than uncomplicated tension-type headache?
option_A: Bilateral pressure-like pain without nausea or light sensitivity
option_B: Mild scalp tightness without associated sensory symptoms
option_C: A non-pulsating headache without nausea or sensory sensitivity
option_D: Headache accompanied by nausea and sensitivity to light
explanation_or_correction: Nausea and sensitivity to light are common migraine-associated symptoms. Pressure-like pain without these features is more typical of a tension-type headache, although patterns can overlap.
reviewer_comment: The level of difficulty for this question could be improved by having less obviously incorrect answers.

text: Why is it inaccurate to judge migraine only by how much head pain a person reports?
option_A: Migraine can have associated symptoms and variable patterns
option_B: Pain intensity alone reliably distinguishes migraine from tension-type headache
option_C: Migraine can be recognized only when headache pain is severe and one-sided
option_D: Associated symptoms such as nausea or light sensitivity add nothing to assessment
explanation_or_correction: Migraine experiences vary, and related symptoms may be important.

text: A migraine is always the same as a short, mild tension headache.
explanation_or_correction: Migraine can involve more than head pain and can have distinctive symptoms such as nausea and sensitivity to light or sound.

text: Aura and accompanying symptoms: Recognizing aura, light/sound sensitivity and nausea as possible but not universal features.
Which statement about migraine aura is correct?
option_A: Every person with migraine must experience aura
option_B: Some migraines include temporary neurological symptoms called aura
option_C: Aura is a type of skin infection
option_D: Aura is the name of a pain medicine
explanation_or_correction: Aura may involve temporary visual or other neurological symptoms before or during some migraines.

text: A student describes gradually spreading zigzag lights that lasted about 20 minutes and then resolved before a headache. Which statement is most appropriate?
option_A: Visual aura can occur only after the headache has ended
option_B: That description proves migraine with aura and excludes other causes
option_C: This could fit visual aura, but new or unusual symptoms still need clinical assessment
option_D: Aura must cause permanent visual loss rather than temporary symptoms
explanation_or_correction: Temporary, spreading visual symptoms can be consistent with migraine aura. A description alone does not establish a diagnosis or rule out other causes, especially when the symptoms are new or unusual.
reviewer_comment: This question and the previous question are almost identical

text: Why should someone discuss new visual or neurological symptoms with a clinician?
option_A: Any brief visual symptom can be assumed to be familiar aura if the person has had headaches before
option_B: Flashing lights alone exclude other neurological causes
option_C: New speech or sensory symptoms never require assessment if they resolve
option_D: Similar symptoms can have more than one cause and may need assessment
explanation_or_correction: New or unusual neurological symptoms should not be assumed to be migraine without appropriate evaluation.

text: Every person with migraine must experience aura.
explanation_or_correction: Some people have migraine with aura, while others have migraine without aura.

text: Triggers and symptom diaries: Individual trigger patterns and recording symptoms without assuming causation.
What is one purpose of a headache diary?
option_A: To record possible patterns, timing and symptoms
option_D: To prove a specific food caused every headache
explanation_or_correction: A diary can help describe patterns for discussion with a care team, but does not prove cause.

text: Which statement about migraine triggers is most accurate?
option_B: Possible triggers differ across people, and patterns may be worth discussing
option_C: A single event proves a trigger for life
explanation_or_correction: Triggers and symptom patterns vary between people.

text: Why should a student avoid claiming a trigger from one diary entry?
option_A: A headache after one late night confirms that sleep loss is the trigger
option_B: A diary entry proves causation whenever symptoms follow a suspected trigger
option_C: One event cannot establish causality, even if symptoms happened afterward
option_D: Keeping a diary automatically removes other possible contributing factors
explanation_or_correction: An isolated association is not enough to establish a cause.

text: A diary entry proves that one particular food caused a migraine.
explanation_or_correction: A diary can identify possible patterns, but temporal association alone does not prove causation.

text: Clinical evaluation and warning changes: The value of professional assessment for new, unusual or changing headaches.
Which statement about changing headache symptoms is most appropriate?
option_A: A sudden major change in headache pattern never needs assessment
option_B: Every headache has one identical cause
option_C: A school quiz always establishes the cause
option_D: A new or noticeably changing headache pattern deserves clinical assessment
explanation_or_correction: New, unusual or changing headaches may need clinical assessment.

text: Why does a clinician ask about the timing and associated symptoms of headache?
option_A: To distinguish possible causes and understand a person's pattern
explanation_or_correction: History and associated symptoms help clinical assessment.

text: What is the safest response to a sudden severe headache with unusual neurological symptoms?
option_A: A past history of migraine makes urgent evaluation unnecessary for any future headache
option_B: Seek urgent medical assessment rather than self-diagnosing from a quiz
option_C: Wait for usual headache medicine to work before seeking care for new neurological symptoms
option_D: Identify a trigger in a headache diary before deciding whether new neurological symptoms require assessment
explanation_or_correction: Sudden severe or unusual neurological symptoms require prompt professional assessment.

text: A sudden major change in a person's headache pattern never needs assessment.
explanation_or_correction: A new, unusual, or markedly changing headache should be discussed with an appropriate healthcare professional; urgent symptoms require prompt attention.

text: General management and self-care planning: Working with a healthcare professional on prevention, symptom management and appropriate follow-up.
What is a sound general approach to migraine management?
option_A: Change medication whenever an online quiz says so
option_B: The same migraine treatment plan works for every person
option_C: Follow an individualized care plan developed with a healthcare professional
option_D: Assume one strategy works for everybody
explanation_or_correction: Management is individual and may include symptom strategies, prevention and clinician follow-up.

text: How can a headache diary assist follow-up care?
option_A: By establishing the diagnosis without any professional assessment
option_B: By showing frequency but not helping evaluate response to treatment
option_C: By replacing medical follow-up if the symptoms seem stable
option_D: By comparing headache frequency and response to the agreed plan over time
explanation_or_correction: Patterns can be discussed with a healthcare professional to review the plan.

text: A person taking a prescribed daily migraine preventive medicine has fewer headaches but bothersome side effects. What is the best next step?
option_A: Review benefits, side effects and possible adjustments with the prescribing clinician
option_B: Reduce the preventive dose independently and mention it at a later visit
option_C: Take the preventive only on headache days despite the daily prescription
option_D: Stop it because fewer headaches prove the preventive is no longer needed
explanation_or_correction: A clinician should review the benefits and adverse effects of preventive treatment before changes are made. Preventive medicines often follow a schedule different from acute headache treatments.
reviewer_comment: Again the question itself is fine but for a question marked as advanced the answers make this a very easy question to answer.

text: The same treatment plan works for every person with migraine.
explanation_or_correction: Migraine management is individualized and should be reviewed with a healthcare professional.
